description: OpenTitan UART F5 behavior: the sticky tx_done event on intr_tx_done_o, the INTR_STATE word the ISR reads, and the one-write W1C acknowledge. The clear is stated as an ordered clear_sequence with one write step, which is the executor's single clear write.
notes: facts read from third_party/soc-opentitan/hw/ip/uart/rtl/uart_core.sv and uart_reg_pkg.sv: INTR_STATE 0 (rw, w1c), INTR_ENABLE 4 (rw), INTR_TEST 8 (wo), CTRL 16 (rw), WDATA 28 (wo, pushes the TX FIFO)

source_port intr_tx_done_o is the RTL's own output port (uart.sv:45) and source_bit_offset 0 is bit 0 of that one-bit port; the profile row for role tx_done declares exactly this alias, active high, level

the INTR_STATE/INTR_ENABLE bit is NOT the port bit and the profile does not state it: uart_reg_pkg.sv's uart_hw2reg_intr_state_reg_t lists the nine fields tx_empty, rx_parity_err, rx_timeout, rx_break_err, rx_frame_err, rx_overflow, tx_done, rx_watermark, tx_watermark, and a packed struct's first field is its MSB, so tx_done is bit 2, tx_watermark bit 0, rx_watermark bit 1 and tx_empty bit 8. The F2 probe of INTR_STATE at reset read 0x101 (tx_watermark and tx_empty, the two status-type bits that are true while the FIFOs are empty), which is what confirms the order

intr_tx_done is one of the six Event-type sources (uart_core.sv:443-454, prim_intr_hw default IntrT="Event"), so an event sets INTR_STATE bit 2 and it stays set until software writes 1 to that bit. The three Status-type sources (tx_watermark, tx_empty, rx_watermark) follow live FIFO conditions and a W1C write cannot deassert them, which is why they are not the declared source

trigger_writes: INTR_ENABLE(4)=4 unmasks tx_done only, CTRL(16)=0xffff0001 enables the transmitter and sets NCO=0xffff so the 16x baud tick runs almost every clock (uart_core.sv:164-177; with NCO=0 the tick never fires and tx_done could not occur), and WDATA(28)=0x5a pushes one byte into the TX FIFO. tx_enable = ctrl.tx (uart_core.sv:77) and the FIFO is popped when the transmitter is idle, so the byte is really serialized and event_tx_done really pulses (uart_core.sv:328)

clear_sequence is [{"kind": "write", "offset": 0, "value": 4}]: the handler writes 1 to INTR_STATE bit 2 and the event latch clears. Because the event is a one-cycle pulse the line stays low afterwards; that is the difference from the timer, whose level is re-asserted while its condition holds

the RX pin is held idle (1) by the scenario's fixed input and CTRL enables only the transmitter, so no RX event can set another INTR_STATE bit during F5; the status-type bits are left masked by INTR_ENABLE=4

this file states device facts only: the executor cross-checks them against configs/peripherals/opentitan_uart_local/component_profile.json, and the declaration does not prove the RTL raises the event (the real F5 run is the evidence)
